title: Compute label parent paths and keys from frame stack at parse time, not by string-splitting paths
context: Kubernetes label keys legitimately contain dots (app.kubernetes.io/instance), which become indistinguishable from path nesting once folded into dot-joined strings. Attempts to extract keys by slicing the joined path were ambiguous: dotted keys were silently rejected, and mismatched dotted values falsely appeared to match on the plain-key remainder alone.
decision: FieldPathEntry now carries parentPath and key computed structurally from the scanner's frame stack at push time, rather than re-derived by string-splitting the output path. extractLiteralLabelMap matches on parentPath exactly, preserving dotted keys and their values intact.
consequences: Dotted label keys (app.kubernetes.io/instance) are now extracted and preserved correctly
False-positive references edges from mismatched dotted-key values no longer occur
The helm create default selector convention (all-dotted keys) is now correctly handled
Parse-time structural data is now authoritative; string re-parsing is eliminated as an error source
alternatives_rejected: Escaping or encoding dots in the joined path string (would require a decoding scheme and would still lose nesting info)
Using array-based path representation throughout (would require refactoring path serialization end-to-end)
Heuristics to detect 'real' vs 'nested' dots from the string alone (inherently ambiguous and fragile)
